title: The pleiotropic effects of a single transcription factor underpin trade-offs associated with insecticide resistance in whitefly.
authors: Huang, Mingjiao; Liu, Shaonan; Fu, Buli; Gong, Peipan; Wu, Xiaojie; Yin, Cheng; Xue, Hu; Yang, Jing; Tan, Qimei; Liu, Yating; Yang, Xin; Zhang, Youjun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究烟粉虱中转录因子E75调控杀虫剂抗性与生殖适合度权衡，涉及TF-DNA结合（EMSA）和分子对接/动力学模拟，但核心是昆虫生理与抗性进化，非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法应用浅层。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The evolution of insecticide resistance is often accompanied by fitness costs on life-history traits; however, the genetic mechanisms underlying this 'benefit-cost' trade-offs remain limited. OBJECTIVES: Here, we aim to elucidate the molecular basis of fitness trade-offs associated with P450-mediated insecticide resistance. METHODS: Insecticide bioassay and life-table methodology were used to determine thiacloprid resistance and its associated fitness cost in the whitefly Bemisia tabaci MED, a notorious pest of crops worldwide. Reverse genetics, western blots, immunofluorescence, molecular docking and dynamics simulation, recombinant P450 enzymes and UPLC-MS/MS were performed to demonstrate the role of the P450 CYP6EM1 in thiacloprid resistance. Dual-luciferase reporter assays, Phos-tag, EMSA, yeast one-hybrid and immunoprecipitation assay were conducted to investigate the role of a transcription factor in regulating the fitness trade-offs between thiacloprid resistance and the associated fitness cost. RESULTS: Here, we uncover that a single transcription factor, Ecdysone-induced protein 75 (E75), underpins trade-offs associated with thiacloprid resistance in the whitefly. We demonstrate that the transmembrane G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) Neuropeptide FF receptor 2 (NPFF2) triggers the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) p38 and ERK signaling pathways, which then promote phosphorylation of E75. This GPCR-E75 regulatory axis not only activates the P450 gene CYP6EM1 but also represses a key oogenesis gene Bg, thereby contributing to the evolution of thiacloprid resistance at the expense of reproductive fitness in the whitefly. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate a pivotal role of cis-trans regulatory networks in fitness trade-offs mediated by GPCR-MAPK-E75 signaling, providing in-depth insights into developing effective measures for sustainable pest control.
abstract_zh: 引言：杀虫剂抗性的演化通常伴随着生活史性状的适应性代价；然而，这种“收益-代价”权衡背后的遗传机制仍知之甚少。目的：本文旨在阐明与P450介导的杀虫剂抗性相关的适应性权衡的分子基础。方法：采用杀虫剂生物测定和生命表方法，测定烟粉虱Bemisia tabaci MED（一种全球作物重要害虫）对噻虫啉的抗性及其相关适应性代价。通过反向遗传学、Western blot、免疫荧光、分子对接和动力学模拟、重组P450酶及UPLC-MS/MS，验证P450 CYP6EM1在噻虫啉抗性中的作用。采用双荧光素酶报告基因实验、Phos-tag、EMSA、酵母单杂交和免疫沉淀实验，研究转录因子在调控噻虫啉抗性与相关适应性代价之间权衡中的作用。结果：本研究发现，单一转录因子蜕皮激素诱导蛋白75（E75）支撑了烟粉虱中与噻虫啉抗性相关的权衡。我们证明，跨膜G蛋白偶联受体（GPCR）神经肽FF受体2（NPFF2）触发丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）p38和ERK信号通路，进而促进E75的磷酸化。这一GPCR-E75调控轴不仅激活P450基因CYP6EM1，还抑制关键卵子发生基因Bg，从而以牺牲烟粉虱生殖适应性为代价，促进噻虫啉抗性的演化。结论：我们的发现证明了顺式-反式调控网络在GPCR-MAPK-E75信号介导的适应性权衡中的关键作用，为制定可持续害虫防治的有效措施提供了深入见解。
